actions.message:
All 4 failing tests in e2e/sound-motion.spec.ts are test bugs, not product bugs. The game state assertions (flag placed, mines revealed, data-exploded set) all pass — the product works correctly. Fix each:

1. **[R27] line 129**: Your board string `......,*.....,......,......,..**..,......` has a mine at row 1 col 0 (the `*` in the second row's first position). Your own comment says '(1,0) is a "1" with no zero neighbours → single-cell reveal'. Clicking it loses the game. Fix the board so (1,0) is actually a numbered safe cell adjacent to exactly one mine. Re-verify every cell the test interacts with against the actual layout.

2. **[R30] lines 227-254**: On BOARD_5 (`*....,.....,.....,.....,.....`), clicking (3,3) cascades through all 24 non-mine cells → instant WIN. The product correctly calls `celebrate()` not `rippleReveal()`. Pick a board where the zero-region cascade reveals multiple cells but does NOT clear all non-mine cells (so the game stays 'playing'). For example a 6×6 or larger board with 2-3 mines placed so the cascade region is a proper subset.

3. **[R31] lines 256-267 & [R32] lines 269-285**: Your `clickAndCapture` helper does everything inside one `page.evaluate` and polls `document.getAnimations()`, but it captures 0 animations in all three motion tests. The product code (src/ui/animation.ts) correctly calls `el.animate(...)` — the issue is your capture method. Instead, use the same spy pattern as `installSpies`: monkey-patch `Element.prototype.animate` via `page.addInitScript` BEFORE page load to record every animation call (target, delay, duration) into a window variable. Then after the interaction, read that record via `page.evaluate`. This is more reliable than polling `document.getAnimations()` inside the same evaluate that triggered the click. The existing `installSpies` already patches `Element.prototype.animate` and records into `window.__anims` — reuse that for R30/R31/R32 instead of `clickAndCapture`.

Also: the T1 finding about `BOARD_TWO_MINES` is stale (already removed). Ensure `npm run lint` passes on your files when you're done.

8. **Win.** When the game is `won`, every mine is flagged.

9. **Flags.** `toggleFlag` flags or unflags a hidden cell; on a revealed cell
   it changes nothing. There may be more flags than mines.

10. **Chord.** `chord` on a revealed cell whose number equals the count of
    flagged neighbours reveals every hidden, unflagged neighbour, exactly as
    `reveal` would (flood included, and a wrong flag can lose the game).
    `lastRevealed` measures `distance` from the chorded cell, which is 0 but
    not itself newly revealed. Otherwise `chord` changes nothing.

11. `minesLeft` is `mines` minus the number of flagged cells; it can be
    negative.

| `#board` | `role="grid"`; contains one `role="row"` per row, each holding one `<button role="gridcell">` per cell; shown as the familiar Minesweeper field -- each row's cells side by side on one line, rows stacked top to bottom, so the cells of a column line up |

| each cell button | `data-row`, `data-col` (0-based); `data-state` is `hidden`, `flagged`, `revealed`, `mine` (a revealed mine) or `wrong-flag` (after a loss, a flag on a non-mine); the mine that lost the game also has `data-exploded="true"`; a revealed cell with `adjacent > 0` has that number as its text, otherwise no text; an `aria-label` that says the cell's position and state |
| `#status` | `data-status` is the game's status; its text tells the player what is going on |
| `#mines-left` | `minesLeft`, as text (`-2` when over-flagged) |
| `#timer` | whole seconds since the first reveal, as text; `0` before; stops when the game ends; never above `999` |
| `#new-game` | a button: a fresh game of the same kind (same difficulty, or the same `?board`) |
| `#difficulty` | a `<select>` with options `beginner`, `intermediate`, `expert`; changing it starts a new game of that size; the choice is remembered across reloads |
| `#best-time` | the fastest win for the current board, in whole seconds, or `—` (an em dash) if there is none; kept across reloads |
| `#mute` | a button, `aria-pressed="true"` when muted; muted state is remembered across reloads; unmuted by default |

- **Mouse:** left click reveals; right click toggles a flag (no browser menu
  appears); left click on a revealed number chords.

- **Keyboard:** the board is one Tab stop — exactly one cell has
  `tabindex="0"`, the rest `-1`. Arrow keys move focus between cells and stop
  at the edges. Enter or Space reveals the focused cell, or chords it if it is
  a revealed number; `F` toggles its flag. Focus is always visible.

- **State is immediate.** Cell `data-state`, `#mines-left`, `#status` and the
  rest change in the same task as the input that changed them — never after
  an animation.

- **Best times** are kept per board: per difficulty, and per `?board` value.
  A win is recorded when it beats the stored time.

- `?board=` fixes the board: rows separated by `,`, each a string of `*`
  (mine) and `.` (safe) — `?board=*....,.....,.....,.....,.....`. The game
  uses that layout (rule 3), and `#new-game` starts it again.

- `?seed=` with an integer makes a random game repeatable (rule 4), at the
  current difficulty.

- With neither, the board is random at the remembered difficulty
  (beginner the first time).
- Every sound is synthesised with the Web Audio API — no audio files.

- Distinct sounds for: revealing one cell, a cascade (one reveal that opens
  more than one cell), placing a flag, removing a flag, a chord, an
  explosion (loss), and a win — the win is a short melody of at least three
  notes.

- **No sound before the player acts:** no `AudioContext` is created before
  the first click or key press on the page.
- **Muted means silent:** while muted, no sound starts at all.

- **Reveal ripple.** Every newly revealed cell animates in (100–600 ms),
  starting `distance × step` after the input, with a fixed step of 15–40 ms,
  so a cascade ripples outward from the click. No cell starts later than
  1000 ms after the input.
- **Flag.** Placing a flag animates.

- **Loss.** The exploded mine animates (a flash, a shake), and the other
  mines appear one after another rather than all at once.
- **Win.** The board or the status celebrates.

- **Reduced motion.** When the user prefers reduced motion, nothing animates
  and nothing transitions: no CSS animations, no CSS transitions, no Web
  Animations.

Pure logic: no DOM, no timers, no `Math.random` except as described for
`seed`. These exports, with these names and shapes:

1. **Immutable.** No function changes the `Game` it is given. A call that
   changes nothing returns the very same object it was given.

2. **Sizes.** `rows` and `cols` are integers from 5 to 50, and `mines` from 1
   to `rows × cols − 9`. Anything else makes `createGame` throw a `RangeError`.

3. **Layout.** With `layout`, the board is exactly that grid: `rows`, `cols`
   and `mines` come from it (any given are ignored), mines never move, and
   `adjacent` is set from the start. The size rule still applies.

4. **Placement.** Without `layout`, mines are placed at the first `reveal`:
   exactly `mines` of them, never on the revealed cell or any of its
   neighbours. With a `seed`, the placement depends only on the seed, the
   board size and the first cell. Until placement every cell has
   `adjacent: 0` and `mine: false`.

5. **Status.** `ready` until the first reveal, then `playing`; `lost` when a
   mine is revealed; `won` when every non-mine cell is revealed (flags are not
   needed). Once `won` or `lost`, every function returns the game unchanged.

6. **Reveal.** Revealing a hidden, unflagged cell reveals it. If it has
   `adjacent: 0`, its neighbours are revealed too, and so on outward: the
   connected region of zero cells and the numbered cells bordering it
   (8-neighbour connectivity). Flagged cells are never revealed this way.
   `lastRevealed` lists every cell the call revealed, each with its
   `distance`: 0 for the clicked cell, otherwise the fewest steps from the
   clicked cell to it, moving one neighbour at a time and passing only
   through revealed zero cells. Revealing a revealed or flagged cell changes
   nothing.

7. **Loss.** Revealing a mine reveals every mine, and the game is `lost`.
   Flags stay where they are.
